top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct, mature invention: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the first-order light shift so many atoms are probed in the Lamb-Dicke regime. It has been realized at about 1e-18 and independently confirmed across laboratories and fibre links, with the gravitational redshift resolved over a millimetre. The Katori (invention) and Ye (realization) allocation is clean and uncontested, and a citation narrowed to the neutral-atom lattice keeps it distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes.
